column1: # check-registry.tsv — the machine-readable inventory of this repository's checks.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# specs/001-workshop-curriculum-platform/spec.md states two success criteria that
# are universally quantified over "every automated check in the feature":
#   SC-012  Every automated check has a paired demonstration that it FAILS when
#           the guarded condition is broken — 100%, no exceptions.
#   SC-013  The system distinguishes "unable to verify" from "passed" and
#           "failed" in 100% of its checks.
# Neither can be evaluated without an enumeration of "every check". A claim
# quantified over a set that does not exist cannot be measured, and per §11.4
# a PASS without positive evidence is a bluff. This file IS that set, and
# scripts/verify-check-registry.sh is the meta-check that walks it.
# It is not decorative. The meta-check closes the enumeration in BOTH
# directions: every row must point at a real file, and every `*.sh` file under
# a declared `scanroot` must appear in some row. A check added to scripts/ and
# not registered here is a FAILURE, not an omission — that is the anti-drift
# half, and without it a registry silently rots into fiction.
# TAB-separated. Field 1 is the ROW TYPE, drawn from a CLOSED vocabulary:
#   scanroot   <dir>
#   exempt     <path>   <reason>   <lifting_authority>  <lifting_evidence>  <next_review>  <fact_sha256>
#   check      <id>  <entry-point>  <proof-kind>  <proof-arg>  <undet-probe>
#   debt       <id>  <entry-point>  <owed>  <reason>  <lifting_authority>  <lifting_evidence>  <next_review>  <fact_sha256>
# An unrecognised field-1 token is a MALFORMED registry and makes the meta-check
# exit 2 (could not determine) — never 0. Comment (`#`) and blank lines are
# inert: the parser keys on field 1, which no "#"-prefixed line can match.
# ── SCHEMA MIGRATION, 2026-09-15 (unified T111 + T116, one coherent change) ──
# `exempt` and `debt` rows are this registry's DECLARED CONDITIONS — a row
# asserting "this is not a defect needing a fix" rather than "this defect is
# absent". FR-007/SC-015 (unified T111) requires a declared condition to name
# WHO may lift it and WHAT EVIDENCE would lift it; FR-027 (unified T116)
# requires it to carry a re-verification cadence and to be flagged when the
# fact it cites has itself moved. Both land as ONE schema change, not two, so
# the two column sets cannot drift out of sync with each other:
#   lifting_authority   a ROLE, never a named individual (this project's
#                       convention throughout — "operator", not a person).
#   lifting_evidence    free text: the CONCRETE change that would make this
#                       row's classification wrong and force it to be
#                       re-registered as a check or promoted out of debt.
#   next_review         an ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). scripts/verify-check-
#                       registry.sh FAILS a row whose next_review has elapsed
#                       — "declared" does not mean "declared once, forever".
#   fact_sha256         sha256 of the row's own file (its `path` for exempt,
#                       its `entry-point` for debt) AS OF THE LAST TIME A
#                       HUMAN OR AGENT VERIFIED THIS ROW'S REASON. The
#                       meta-check re-hashes the file on every run and FAILS
#                       when it no longer matches: the row's stated FACT has
#                       moved and the reason was not re-read against the new
#                       content. This is not hypothetical — the reason on the
#                       `_tools/watch-deploy.sh` row below already changed
#                       once, on 2026-09-08, because the file grew a verdict
#                       the row's older text did not describe. A content-hash
#                       mismatch is exactly the shape of that event, generic
#                       across every declared-condition row instead of relying
#                       on someone happening to notice.
# `check` rows are unaffected: a check is ACTIVELY re-verified every run (its
# paired proof, its rc-2 probe), so it is not a "declared" condition in the
# sense these columns exist for.
# WHY TSV AND NOT YAML. Three reasons, in order of weight:
#   1. It is this project's existing convention for exactly this artefact.
#      The governance submodule keeps every gate ledger as TSV —
#      submodules/constitution/scripts/gates/{gate_ledger_deferrals,
#      gate_first_refusal,rule_seam_bindings,mutation_score_kill_map,
#      covenant_propagation_anchors}.tsv — all parsed with `cut -f1`. Inventing
#      a second ledger dialect for the same job would be the drift this file
#      exists to prevent.
#   2. Typed rows from a closed vocabulary are already a governance requirement
#      here: submodules/constitution/scripts/gates/cm_ledger_row_typed_from_
#      closed_vocabulary.sh enforces the shape this file uses.
#   3. It parses with `IFS=$'\t' read` and nothing else. helix-deps.yaml is the
#      right home for SUBMODULE PINS and is read by a Python-assisted script;
#      a pre-push instrument must not acquire a python3/yq dependency to answer
#      "is every check proved?". A parser that can fail to load is a parser that
#      can report a green tree it never read.
# scanroot <dir>
#     Repo-relative directory swept for `*.sh`. Every file found must be
#     accounted for by a check, debt, or exempt row. Missing directory -> rc 2.
# exempt <path> <reason> <lifting_authority> <lifting_evidence> <next_review> <fact_sha256>
#     A `*.sh` under a scanroot that is NOT a check (an installer, a mutator, a
#     remediation tool). The reason is mandatory and free text. This mirrors the
#     `.hardcoded-paths-allow` convention already used at this root: an
#     exemption always carries its justification inline. The four trailing
#     fields are the 2026-09-15 schema migration described above.
# check <id> <entry-point> <proof-kind> <proof-arg> <undet-probe>
#     A check asserted to satisfy BOTH SC-012 and SC-013.
#       id           stable ASCII slug, unique across the file
#       entry-point  repo-relative path; must exist AND be executable
#       proof-kind   `flag`    the entry point itself runs its paired proof
#                    `sibling` a separate `*_mutation_test.sh` runs it
#       proof-arg    for `flag`:    the argv that invokes the proof; it MUST be
#                                   a real `case` arm in the entry point
#                    for `sibling`: repo-relative path to the proof script
#       undet-probe  argv (optionally prefixed with `VAR=value` assignments)
#                    that MUST drive the entry point to exit 2. Every `--flag`
#                    token in it must be a real `case` arm — a probe that only
#                    trips the unknown-option handler proves nothing, because
#                    "bad usage" is not "unable to verify". The meta-check
#                    rejects such a probe rather than crediting it.
# debt <id> <entry-point> <owed> <reason> <lifting_authority> <lifting_evidence> <next_review> <fact_sha256>
#     A REGISTERED, non-conforming check. `owed` is a comma-separated subset of
#     {proof, three-valued, executable} naming which property is missing. The
#     four trailing fields are the 2026-09-15 schema migration described above.
#     Modelled directly on §11.4.227(A)'s registered-deferral ledger
#     (submodules/constitution/scripts/gates/gate_ledger_deferrals.tsv): silent
#     debt is forbidden, so debt is DECLARED and counted rather than hidden by
#     omission or excused by a green exit.
#     Debt does not block a default run — it prints a loud DEBT block and the
#     run still exits 0, the same shape `scripts/pre-push-gates.sh` uses for its
#     stated-reason SKIPs. `--strict` turns every debt row into a FAIL (rc 1).
#     A DEBT row is NOT compliance and must never be reported as one.
#     Debt is also RATCHETED: if a debt row's owed property is found to be
#     SATISFIED, that is a FAILURE ("stale debt — promote it to a check row").
#     Debt can hide a gap; it must not be able to hide a fix.
# Determined empirically on 2026-09-01 by running each entry point, not by
# reading its prose. Re-derive, do not trust undated:
#     bash scripts/verify-check-registry.sh              # structural, seconds
#     bash scripts/verify-check-registry.sh --run-proofs # also executes proofs
#     bash scripts/verify-check-registry.sh --strict     # debt becomes failure
#     bash scripts/verify-check-registry.sh --prove-failure   # its own §1.1 proof
# WIDENED 2026-09-06. The scanroots were `scripts/` and `tests/` only, and this
# block used to record why: `_tools/` and `_tests/` hold further gates that
# scripts/pre-push-gates.sh runs, and they were "NOT swept here yet ... because
# those trees were under concurrent edit". `_tools/` no longer is, so it is
# swept now — `_tools`, `_tools/translate` and `_tools/portfolio` are declared
# below and the three gates the old note named by hand are registered as `check`
# rows, each with a paired §1.1 proof and a demonstrated rc-2 state that were
# WRITTEN for this change, not merely asserted. What each one owed, and what it
# was measured doing before it was fixed, is recorded in the row comments.
# `_tests/` IS STILL NOT SWEPT, and `_tests/run-harness-selfvalidation.sh` is
# therefore still unregistered. That is unchanged and deliberate: that tree was
# under concurrent edit while this change was made, so nothing in it was read,
# run, or judged. It is a DECLARED boundary, not a claim of conformance.
# The sweep is `find -maxdepth 1`, so a scanroot covers ONE directory level.
# SEVEN `*.sh` under `_tools/` therefore remain outside it, in five further
# subdirectories that are not declared as scanroots:
#   _tools/containers/compose/jekyll-build.sh   _tools/gen/build.sh
#   _tools/containers/compose/ocr-run.sh        _tools/helixtranslate-container/run.sh
#   _tools/od/generate.sh                       _tools/od/start-daemon.sh
#   _tools/pdf/build-pdfs.sh
# The count above read SIX until 2026-09-08 and was measured wrong, not merely
# stale: `_tools/containers/compose/ocr-run.sh` landed with the OCR workload and
# was never added to this list. That is exactly the drift this block exists to
# prevent, so the correction is recorded rather than silently applied. Both
# `compose/` entries stay outside `_tools/containers` (declared a scanroot in
# the same change) because maxdepth 1 does not reach a second level. Re-derive
# instead of trusting the list:
#   find _tools -name '*.sh' -type f  |  filter out the four declared scanroots
# Naming them here is the point: an undeclared boundary is the thing this file
# exists to prevent. The same maxdepth rule already applies to `scripts/audit/`
# and `scripts/badges/`, whose checks are registered individually.
scanroot
scanroot
scanroot
scanroot
scanroot
scanroot
# ── Files under a scanroot that are not checks ───────────────────────────────
exempt

# push-topology — registered 2026-09-06, and it closes a measured blind spot
# rather than a hypothetical one. `git grep -- '--all --push'` returned NOTHING
# in the entire tree that day: every remote-aware instrument here reads either
# `.gitmodules` (which carries ONE url per submodule, and it is a FETCH url) or

# `.git/config`, so a fan-out configured there was invisible to all of them.

# push urls include gitflic.ru and gitverse.ru, hosts for which no read-only API
# adapter is registered, so their visibility cannot be established. Its
# --prove-failure battery is 11 assertions over 10 fixture trees, every mutation
# DATA (a seeded git remote configuration plus a PATH-shimmed provider answering
# from a fixture table), and M1 exists solely to keep `git remote get-url --push`
# — which prints only the FIRST of six — out of the implementation.

column3: deploy driver: regenerates both sites, commits and pushes them, then validates the LIVE sites. It MUTATES two production repositories, and it remains a producer rather than a check OF THIS REPOSITORY — the sweep may not run it, because running it publishes to two live sites. THE OLD REASON'S CLOSING CLAUSE — "its output is a deployment, not a judgement about this tree" — IS WITHDRAWN as of 2026-09-08, and the row is kept exempt on the narrower ground above rather than on that one. What changed: commit 738fbf1 (2026-09-08) added a BUILD GATE to this script that judges this repository's own build steps and ABORTS the deploy before anything is staged, committed or pushed. Until that commit every build step ended in `|| build_warn`, which only incremented a counter, so `--dry-run` printed success having built nothing. It is now three-valued and the contract is written into the source: build_warn -> tolerated, exit unchanged; build_fail -> exit 5 (ran and failed); build_undet -> exit 2 (could not run), with FAIL outranking UNDET so an absent toolchain can never launder a real failure. It ships its own §1.1 paired battery, `bash _tools/deploy-langs.sh --prove-build-fatality`, which drives every branch through the pure `build_gate` function without building, staging, committing or pushing. So this file DOES now judge, and the exemption's ground has moved from "it judges nothing" to "it may not be executed by a sweep"; re-validated by reading the source on 2026-09-08. HONEST BOUNDARY: that proof was NOT executed during this re-validation — running a live production deploy driver was out of scope for the exemption audit that found this — so the verdict rests on reading lines 226-300 and 370 of the file, not on a captured run. The live-site verdict (classify_live_result, exit 1/2/0) is OLDER than today and was already about the deployed sites rather than about this tree; it is not what expired this row Re-verified 2026-09-22: the jekyll step gained a THIRD runner (the containerised _tools/containers/bin/site-build) used only when neither host `jekyll` nor `bundle exec jekyll` works; its exit is mapped onto the same three-valued build gate (1 -> build_fail, 2 -> build_undet), and --prove-build-fatality still passes 7 assertions. Classification unchanged. Re-verified 2026-09-26: the fact_sha256 drift was a real, legitimate edit (fix-rebuild-traps, T025 build-if-missing) — the site-build rebuild trigger at line ~671 changed from existence-only to existence-or-stale (find -newer), with a new explanatory comment block; the BUILD GATE's own three-valued contract (build_warn/build_fail/build_undet, case 0/1/*) and everything this row's reason describes are UNCHANGED, independently reviewed (rev-rebuild: ACCEPT).

column1: # ── _tools/ gates — registered 2026-09-06, each fixed before it was registered ─
# scripts/pre-push-gates.sh has run all three since long before the registry
# existed (gate_2, gate_3, gate_4). Being run by the hook is not conformance,
# and the audit that preceded this registration found that two of the three
# were not three-valued in the direction they claimed. What each owed, and the
# measurement that established it, is recorded on the row.
# hardcoded-content — a MISSING GO TOOLCHAIN already returned 2 (measured with a
# PATH-stubbed `go`), but every OTHER "the gate had no input" path returned 1
# while printing the words "gate could not run": driven with a stub `go` that
# built a generator emitting nothing, it printed "❌ FAIL — gate could not run"
# and exited 1. An unusable build was reported as a confirmed hardcoding
# violation. die() is now rc 2, and the gate gained --audit-only (which is what
# lets its proof drive the shipped code path against fixture trees) and a
# --prove-failure battery of 9 data-only mutations.
check
# translate-reproducibility — BOTH halves of this gate are ABSENCE assertions,
# and an absence assertion over an empty set is vacuously true. The shell half
# had a positive control; the PYTHON half did not. Driven on a throwaway copy
# with every *.py under _tools deleted, it printed "PASS (no /tmp engine default
# in any _tools/**/*.py)" and exited 0 — a pass for a population it no longer
# had. It now proves its subject is non-empty before asserting over it, has a
# real rc 2, and carries a 5-mutation --prove-failure battery whose M4 is
# exactly that vacuous pass.
check
# portfolio-data-integrity — this one was already three-valued for the fixture
# faults its own header documents (deleted and corrupt golden-BAD fixtures both
# measured rc 2 before any change). It had ONE hole: run_case mapped any rc
# outside {0,1,2} to UNDETERMINED in the evidence JSON, but the assertion block
# re-tested the raw rc and sent everything else to FAIL. With `node` hidden
# behind a PATH stub it exited 1 saying "validator is not mutation-paired"
# while its own evidence recorded UNDETERMINED. Both arms now branch on the
# same vocabulary, and the 8-mutation --prove-failure battery includes that
# case (M8) and an out-of-contract validator (M6).
# The rc-2 probe is `--fixtures /nonexistent`, and the subject guard is ordered
# BEFORE the evidence-directory mkdir on purpose: the default OUT is tracked
# evidence under _tests/, so a probe that ran past that point would dirty the
# working tree every time the registry is verified.
check
check

# the FR-009 two-number statement (defect vs declared-condition reds, never

# threshold-principles — T112 (unified 005/T034). Asserts FR-010 mechanically:
# a git diff that changes a numeric threshold/baseline/allow-list literal
# must also touch a principle marker (a REASON:/BASELINE: comment, or a
# derived-formula shape) in the SAME diff, or it is flagged. A heuristic by
# its own header's admission — it reads what changed in the diff BODY, never
# a commit message — but it is the first instrument in this fleet that
# detects the CLASS mechanically rather than relying on two existing guards'
# prose-by-construction discipline.

# ── _tools/ debt — declared, counted, NOT fixed ──────────────────────────────
# review-translations.sh is NOT exempt, and calling it one would have been the

column3: T013 evidence ADAPTER (a writer): runs one check through the constitution recorder (execution_record.sh) and appends one sealed record to a two-file evidence store — a verifier-native 9-field chain produced by upstream chain.ExecRow.ToRecord and linked by chain.Digest, plus a sidecar validated against contracts/evidence-record.schema.json, bound by artifact_path = sha256 of the exact sidecar line — and one strict FR-045 row to exec_rows.jsonl that upstream DecodeExecRows reads. Store + streams live untracked under .remember/logs/zero-gap/evidence (operator ruling). It MUTATES a store rather than asserting a verdict about this repository; judging the store is scripts/zero-gap-evidence-chain.sh's role (registered as a check below). It carries its own §1.1 paired proof (--prove-failure, 37 cases on throwaway stores, streams and work trees: outcome is the check's own verdict, never an exit code alone; a moved state fingerprint forces outcome 2; digests cover the FULL stream before truncation; streams are redacted before storage by the upstream scanner, a stream over the scan size cap or time bound is replaced whole with a placeholder naming that cause; the command line is refused BEFORE the command runs, with nothing written, when (a) the argv NAME/SHAPE policy (zg-chain argv-policy, one process) matches any argument or any whitespace-separated WORD inside one AFTER normalisation — shell quotes removed, $'…' / \xHH / \uHHHH / octal escapes decoded, other \c read as c, zero-width characters dropped, full-width ASCII folded, Cyrillic/Greek look-alike letters folded onto Latin when a name is judged, a name mixing Latin with Cyrillic/Greek refused as a look-alike — so '--password', "--password", \--password, $'--pass\x77ord', -''p and --раssword read as their plain form: a flag whose name, or a KEY in any key=value / key:value segment split on = : , ; & ? INCLUDING a flag's value and a URL query (--build-arg=TOKEN=, --header=Cookie:s=, --opt=a:b,token=, --set=db.password=, ?access_token=, ?key=), contains secret/password/passwd/passphrase/token/apikey/api-key/api_key/credential/cookie/authoriz, has a segment that is pw, starts with pass/pwd or ends in pass/pwd (db-pass, DB_PASS, MYSQL_PWD, storepass, keypass), or is key or a qualified key (access-key, secret_key, apikey); -p/-pVALUE and -P/-PVALUE; -u/--user with a user:password value; Authorization:; Bearer <word>; scheme://user:pass@host and the token-only scheme://TOKEN@host (git@ exempt) — or (b) the upstream scanner finds a credential in argv/cwd (per argument, windows of three, name=value pairs). NOT caught (stated in the header, registered as an upstream limitation): a NAME-LESS value — redis-cli -a X (-a is refused by no rule; recipe REDISCLI_AUTH), a positional or bare secret; obfuscated, encoded or computed secrets (base64, piped or read at run time); the scheme-less ssh user@host form; and on STREAMS the upstream scanner alone applies, which misses token=, pass:, bare Bearer, URL credentials and short passwords. Accepted false positives: every -p…/-P… single-dash option (go test -p 1: use GOFLAGS=-p=1 or a wrapper script; grep -P, mysql -P, scp -P, rsync -P), --passes, --max-tokens, --key and any KEY=value segment, a legitimate username in a URL (https://alice@host). UPSTREAM LIMITATION (registered): the recorder forks sed/tr/sed per argument, so a 3000-argument record takes ~31 s of which ~28 s is upstream (the adapter's own gates ~2.3 s; printed as a NOTE by every proof run) — the daily job runs records ONE AT A TIME or sets ZG_LOCK_TIMEOUT above its longest check, because the exclusive store lock is held for the whole record and a parallel sweep gets rc 2 refusals. The exclusive store lock is taken before pre-flight and the run and held through sealing (a lock not obtained within the bound refuses the run: rc 2, not executed, nothing written); the held mode of an inherited lock is read from /proc/self/fdinfo, never from ZG_LOCK_MODE, and no flock is ever issued on an inherited descriptor; a SIGTERM leaves nothing on disk, a SIGKILL remnant is scrubbed by the next run unless the wrapped command still runs; a store failing pre-flight never runs the check; a tracked --verdict-file is never deleted; concurrent appends; 3000 arguments clear both argv gates in < 5 s; every build artefact the shim module can drop inside the repository (zero-gap-chain, *.test, bin/) is git-ignored; the produced store verified by the upstream verifier). Three-valued: 0 every case passed, 1 a case failed, 2 cannot determine (go/jq absent, fixture unbuildable, or the live inputs moved while the proof ran).
column5: the file stops being a writer of evidence records and starts asserting a pass/fail verdict about this repository on its own behalf — that judging role belongs to scripts/zero-gap-evidence-chain.sh
